mn145:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn145:1.3: Then the venerable Puṇṇa, rising from meditation in the evening, went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side. Sitting at one side, the venerable Puṇṇa said to the Blessed One:
mn145:2.1: ‘Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would instruct me in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute.’
mn145:2.2: ‘Then, Puṇṇa, listen and heed well what I shall say.’
mn145:2.3: ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the venerable Puṇṇa replied.
mn145:3.1: ‘Puṇṇa, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.
mn145:3.2: If a bhikkhu relishes, welcomes, and remains holding to that,
mn145:3.3: then, as he relishes, welcomes, and remains holding to it, relishing arises in him.
mn145:3.4: With the arising of relishing, Puṇṇa, there is the arising of suffering, I say.
mn145:3.5: There are sounds cognizable by the ear …
mn145:3.9: dhammas cognizable by the mind that are wished for, desired, agreeable and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.
mn145:3.10: If a bhikkhu relishes, welcomes, and remains holding to that,
mn145:3.11: then, as he relishes, welcomes, and remains holding to it, relishing arises in him.
mn145:3.12: With the arising of relishing, Puṇṇa, there is the arising of suffering, I say.
mn145:4.1: But, Puṇṇa, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.
mn145:4.2: If a bhikkhu does not relish, welcome, or remain holding to that,
mn145:4.3: then, as he does not relish, welcome, or remain holding to it, relishing ceases in him.
mn145:4.4: With the ceasing of relishing, Puṇṇa, there is the ceasing of suffering, I say.
mn145:4.5: There are sounds cognizable by the ear …
mn145:4.9: dhammas cognizable by the mind that are wished for, desired, agreeable and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.
mn145:4.10: If a bhikkhu does not relish, welcome, or remain holding to that,
mn145:4.11: then, as he does not relish, welcome, or remain holding to it, relishing ceases in him.
mn145:4.12: With the ceasing of relishing, Puṇṇa, there is the ceasing of suffering, I say.
mn145:5.1: ‘Now, Puṇṇa, having been given this brief instruction by me, in which country will you dwell?’
mn145:5.2: ‘Venerable sir, having been given this brief instruction by the Blessed One, there is a country called Sunāparanta; I will dwell there.’
mn145:5.3: ‘Fierce, Puṇṇa, are the people of Sunāparanta;
mn145:5.4: rough, Puṇṇa, are the people of Sunāparanta.
mn145:5.5: If the people of Sunāparanta abuse and threaten you, Puṇṇa, what will you think then?’
mn145:5.6: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta abuse and threaten me, then I shall think:
mn145:5.7: “These people of Sunāparanta are good indeed, truly good indeed, in that they do not give me a blow with the fist.”
mn145:5.8: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;
mn145:5.9: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’
mn145:5.10: ‘But, Puṇṇa, if the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with the fist, what will you think then?’
mn145:5.11: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta give me a blow with the fist, then I shall think:
mn145:5.12: “These people of Sunāparanta are good indeed, truly good indeed, in that they do not give me a blow with a clod.”
mn145:5.13: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;
mn145:5.14: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’
mn145:5.15: ‘But, Puṇṇa, if the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with a clod, what will you think then?’
mn145:5.16: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta give me a blow with a clod, then I shall think:
mn145:5.17: “These people of Sunāparanta are good indeed, truly good indeed, in that they do not give me a blow with a stick.”
mn145:5.18: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;
mn145:5.19: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’
mn145:5.20: ‘But, Puṇṇa, if the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with a stick, what will you think then?’
mn145:5.21: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta give me a blow with a stick, then I shall think:
mn145:5.22: “These people of Sunāparanta are good indeed, truly good indeed, in that they do not give me a blow with a knife.”
mn145:5.23: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;
mn145:5.24: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’
mn145:5.25: ‘But, Puṇṇa, if the people of Sunāparanta give you a blow with a knife, what will you think then?’
mn145:5.26: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta give me a blow with a knife, then I shall think:
mn145:5.27: “These people of Sunāparanta are good indeed, truly good indeed, in that they do not deprive me of life with a sharp knife.”
mn145:5.28: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;
mn145:5.29: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’
mn145:5.30: ‘But, Puṇṇa, if the people of Sunāparanta deprive you of life with a sharp knife, what will you think then?’
mn145:5.31: ‘Venerable sir, if the people of Sunāparanta deprive me of life with a sharp knife, then I shall think:
mn145:5.32: “There have been disciples of the Blessed One who, humiliated and disgusted by the body and by life, sought for a knife-bringer. I have found this knife-bringer without seeking him.”
mn145:5.33: That, Blessed One, is what I shall think;
mn145:5.34: that, Sublime One, is what I shall think.’
mn145:6.2: Possessing such self-control and peacefulness, you will be able to dwell in the country of Sunāparanta.
mn145:6.3: Now, Puṇṇa, you may go at your own convenience.’
mn145:7.1: Then the venerable Puṇṇa, having delighted in and rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, and after paying homage to the Blessed One, keeping him on his right, he set his lodging in order, and taking his bowl and outer robe, set out on tour toward the country of Sunāparanta.
mn145:7.2: Wandering on tour by stages, he arrived at the country of Sunāparanta.
mn145:7.3: There the venerable Puṇṇa dwelt in the country of Sunāparanta.
mn145:7.4: Then, within that same rainy season, the venerable Puṇṇa established about five hundred male lay followers and about five hundred female lay followers, and within that same rainy season he himself realized the three true knowledges.
mn145:7.5: Then, after some time, the venerable Puṇṇa attained final Nibbāna.
mn145:8.1: Then a number of bhikkhus went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, they sat down at one side. Sitting at one side, those bhikkhus said to the Blessed One:
mn145:8.2: ‘Venerable sir, the clansman named Puṇṇa, to whom the Blessed One gave brief instruction, has died.
mn145:8.3: What is his destination, what is his future course?’
mn145:8.4: ‘Bhikkhus, the clansman Puṇṇa was wise; he practised in accordance with the Dhamma, and he did not trouble me over the interpretation of the Dhamma.
mn145:8.5: The clansman Puṇṇa, bhikkhus, has attained final Nibbāna.’
mn145:8.6: This is what the Blessed One said.
mn145:8.7: Those bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
mn145:8.8: The Discourse Giving Advice to Puṇṇa, the third, is finished.
